objective: Implement a read-only live Hyperliquid oracle, the single-owner simulator runtime, and seeded local actors for BTC, ETH, and SOL, with activeAssetCtx oraclePx as primary input, metaAndAssetCtxs fallback, deterministic actor behavior, and a 60-second stale-order safety gate.

assertions: The oracle maps only BTC, ETH, and SOL, consumes activeAssetCtx.oraclePx as primary data, falls back to read-only metaAndAssetCtxs, and rejects malformed, non-positive, unmapped, or out-of-order observations without cross-contaminating assets.
At observation age greater than 60 seconds, new user and actor orders for the affected asset are rejected with oracle_stale while cancel and state queries remain available.
The runtime has one engine owner, bounded command/event channels, explicit logical time, and no adapter or actor direct-mutation path.
Given identical seeds, clock steps, and oracle observations, actor commands and resulting core event streams are identical; different asset books remain independent.
A test double proves the upstream surface is read-only and that disconnection/reconnect cannot invoke order, cancel, transfer, wallet, or any other state-changing Hyperliquid method.

deliverables: oracle-hyperliquid read-only client, normalization, health, fallback, and reconnection tests
Single-owner runtime, fake clock, freshness gate, and bounded fan-out plumbing
Seeded synthetic liquidity/trade actors and deterministic tests
risks: Upstream schema drift or symbol ordering can map a price to the wrong local asset.
Wall-clock or unseeded randomness can make actor and event behavior irreproducible.
An overly broad upstream client can violate the no-real-trading safety boundary.
notes: Manifest edits overlap task #2 only for oracle/runtime dependencies. The HTTP scope was added by contract amendment task #17 after task #5 introduced the typed RuntimeError::OracleStale variant inside its original runtime scope and the accepted task #3 adapter's exhaustive match made the merge result fail. HTTP changes in task #5 are limited to mapping typed runtime oracle errors and associated focused regressions; unrelated adapter behavior remains out of scope.
